clue.text: Shrink undergarment? That offers revealing glimpse!

definitions.text: Shrink undergarment? That offers revealing glimpse!

parts.words: Shrink undergarment? That offers revealing glimpse!
parts.note: a shrink is a psychiatrist, so the undergarment a famous one would own is his slip; such a slip of the tongue reveals hidden thoughts

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a piece of lingerie that lets a little too much show.
explanation.walkthrough: The founding psychoanalyst's 'slip' is read as an undergarment, while the real sense is a verbal error that gives away unconscious thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal error thought to expose a speaker's unconscious wishes is named after the father of psychoanalysis.

clue.text: Publish again about children

parts.note: re means about, concerning
issue is a formal word for offspring, children

explanation.surface: An author decides to bring out a new edition of a book about kids.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue a book or record is to bring it out once more.

clue.text: Taboo being mean online but funny

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters are set out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Being nasty on the internet is off-limits, though it may seem amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is too shocking or embarrassing to be spoken of.

clue.text: Winter eavesdropper?

parts.note: read eavesdropper as something that drops from the eaves in cold weather, not a listener

explanation.surface: Someone spies on conversations in the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: An eavesdropper usually listens in secret; here it is a thing hanging and dripping from a roof's eaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike of frozen water forms hanging from roof edges as drips freeze.

clue.text: Citizen with confidence in charitable organisation

parts.note: a national is a citizen of a country
trust is confidence

explanation.surface: A citizen places faith in a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Trust is a major British conservation charity caring for heritage properties.

clue.text: Match not serious

definitions.meaning: a flame, such as a match, for a cigarette
... reading or ... entertainment is not serious

explanation.surface: A game is not being taken seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: A match gives a flame, as in asking for a light; light also means frivolous or trivial.

clue.text: Fish from Asian country served in public house area

indicators.note: served in puts the country inside the pub abbreviation, like food served in a pub

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
Iran is a country in Asia

explanation.surface: A Persian dish is on the menu in a pub's dining space.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a sharp-toothed South American freshwater predator.

clue.text: Great singer takes most of bed

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word for bed is dropped

parts.note: a divan is a type of bed

explanation.surface: A star vocalist hogs the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera star, a leading soprano.

clue.text: I love to wear dumb expression

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it on you, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: dumb means stupid, dim
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they like a silly look on their face.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set phrase or turn of speech, a fixed form of words.

clue.text: Two for one for example in Bury

indicators.note: in places the example abbreviation inside the word for burying

parts.note: to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: A shopping bargain offer is mentioned, apparently set in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two for one' looks like a shop deal; read it as 'two, for one', meaning two is one instance of the answer. Bury is also a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The number two is one instance of a whole number.

clue.text: Stadium beside lake hosts second team

indicators.note: beside puts the lake's letter next to the stadium word
a host takes others in, so the abbreviation for second goes inside

parts.note: an arena is a stadium
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A sports ground by the water plays host to a reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: ARSENAL is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a well-known English football club, a side playing in the Premier League.

clue.text: Regularly seen around in Dunnet Forest

indicators.note: around means the run of letters found is turned to read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words Dunnet Forest

explanation.surface: Something is often spotted in a forest near Dunnet, on Scotland's far north coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to NETFO inside 'Dunnet Forest'; 'around' reads that run backwards. 'seen' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something regularly means doing it frequently, many times over.

clue.text: Maybe Irish agile playing at speed of light

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of agile frolicking into a new order

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: An Irish athlete, perhaps, moves nimbly at blinding pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is one example of the Celtic languages of that family, alongside Scottish and Manx forms.

clue.text: Light source good with volatile plasma

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, so the letters of plasma are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fine light comes from glowing unstable plasma.
explanation.definitionFit: A street or house lamp burning coal gas was a standard illuminator before electricity.

clue.text: Father entertains a deity in shrine

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside, so the father's word encloses the rest

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a deity is a god

explanation.surface: A dad welcomes a god into a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist temple tower, a sacred building.

clue.text: Venezuelan flower for womble

definitions.meaning: a flower here is something that flows, a river
One of the Wombles, furry creatures of a British children's TV series

explanation.surface: A blossom from Venezuela is given to a cuddly creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means something that flows, a river. The Wombles were furry litter-collecting creatures in 1970s British children's books and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American river and a character from the Wimbledon Common children's series share the name.

clue.text: Strong container holds ten

indicators.note: holds means the container word wraps round the number

parts.note: a pot is a container

explanation.surface: A sturdy vessel contains ten items.
explanation.definitionFit: Something potent is powerful, as a forceful drink or drug is.

clue.text: Sons suffering in Catholic country

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for son
suffering is pain

explanation.surface: Boys endure hardship in a devout nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a European nation whose dominant religion has long been Roman Catholicism.

clue.text: Copying brooch in silver

indicators.note: in places the brooch word inside the silver symbol

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pin is a brooch

explanation.surface: Someone copies a jewelled pin set in silver.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate or mimic them.

clue.text: Saint in love with wealthy bird

indicators.note: in places the saint's abbreviation inside the pair of words for love and wealthy
with joins the wealthy word on after the letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A holy man falls for a rich partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African species, the biggest living one of its kind.

clue.text: Dislike seen in clash at Edgbaston

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted inside the words clash at Edgbaston

explanation.surface: Bad feeling surfaces in a match at a famous cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgbaston is a cricket ground in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate is to detest, a strong form of aversion.

clue.text: Friend in Paris clever and approachable

parts.note: ami is French for friend
able means clever, capable

explanation.surface: A Parisian companion is both smart and easy to talk to.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone friendly and pleasant is easy to approach and talk with.

clue.text: Submarine about to disintegrate

indicators.note: to disintegrate is to fall to pieces, so the letters of about are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A submarine is on the point of breaking apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat was a German military undersea vessel of the World Wars.

clue.text: Mate pointing out natural colouring

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the two words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's partner remarks on their skin tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigmentation is the colour of skin, hair or tissue produced by the body's own pigments.
